name: Standing Warm-up
purpose: Gently prepare your body before a short session.
safety: Move gently and within a comfortable range. Stop if you feel pain, dizziness or unusual discomfort.
instructions: March gently on the spot for about 30 seconds.
Roll your shoulders slowly forwards and backwards.
Make small, slow arm circles and gradually let them grow if comfortable.
Shift your weight gently from foot to foot.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Slow down; a warm-up should feel easy.
Stay in a range that feels comfortable and never bounce.

limitations: Guided only. The camera does not score warm-up movements.

name: Bodyweight Squat
purpose: Practise a controlled lower-body movement similar to sitting down and standing up.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Use a comfortable range of motion and a clear, stable floor. Stop if you feel pain or dizziness.
instructions: Stand with feet in a comfortable position.
Keep your whole foot supported.
Bend your hips and knees in a controlled way.
Return to standing without rushing.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Slow down so the way down and the way up are both controlled.
Try a slightly wider stance or a smaller depth that keeps your feet supported.
Check your alignment and try a comfortable stance where your knees travel in line with your toes.

limitations: Camera feedback is educational and may be unavailable for some body shapes, clothing, lighting, and camera angles.

name: Hip Hinge
purpose: Learn to bend forward from the hips while keeping your back long.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear floor, with space behind you.
safety: Move slowly within a comfortable range. Stop if you feel pain in your back or legs.
instructions: Stand with feet about hip-width apart and knees softly bent.
Slide your hips backwards as your chest tips forward.
Keep your back long and your neck relaxed.
Bring your hips forward to return to standing.
commonCues: Move only as far as feels comfortable.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Use a smaller range and keep your chest open.
Keep the knee bend small and let your hips travel backwards.

limitations: Instructional only until camera rules are validated. No automated feedback.

name: Push-up
purpose: Practise a controlled upper-body pushing movement using your own body weight.
space: Floor space for your full body length. A sturdy wall or table works for the easier variation.
safety: Choose a variation appropriate to your ability. Stop if you feel pain or unusual discomfort.
instructions: Set up with hands in a comfortable position.
Keep your body supported.
Lower under control only as far as comfortable.
Push back to the starting position.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Try an easier incline variation with hands on a wall or sturdy table, or lower your knees to the floor.
Lower slowly and only as far as feels comfortable.
Breathe steadily throughout the movement.

limitations: Do not enable automated quality scoring until side-view tracking is validated.

name: Boxing Stance
purpose: Learn a balanced, relaxed starting position used in beginner boxing practice.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear floor. Wear supportive footwear or train on a non-slip surface.
safety: Practise without contact. Keep enough clear space around you. Learn martial arts technique from a qualified instructor.
instructions: Stand in a comfortable staggered stance.
Keep knees relaxed rather than locked.
Bring hands to a comfortable guard position.
Practise returning to a balanced neutral position.
commonCues: Make sure your full body is visible.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Step the feet roughly hip-width apart so you feel stable when shifting your weight.
Keep a slight, relaxed bend in both knees.
Hold the hands near the face in a relaxed guard without squeezing.

limitations: This is a beginner educational guide, not a certification of boxing technique.

name: Jab
purpose: Practise the lead-hand extension slowly, focusing on balance and returning to guard.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly in open space without hitting people or objects. Stop if uncomfortable.
instructions: Begin from a comfortable boxing stance.
Practise a slow, controlled lead-hand extension.
Return the hand to guard.
Reset your balance before repeating.
commonCues: Do not chase speed or power.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the rear hand near your face while the lead hand extends.
Extend smoothly and stop just short of a fully locked elbow.
Stay balanced over your feet; it is fine if the hand does not travel far.

limitations: Do not estimate impact, force, combat effectiveness, or injury risk.

name: Cross
purpose: Practise the rear-hand extension slowly with a controlled turn of the body.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Begin from a comfortable stance.
Watch the 3D demonstration from more than one angle.
Practise a slow, controlled movement.
Return to a balanced stance.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Make the movement smaller and slower until you feel stable.
Bring the hand straight back to your face before the next repetition.
Turn only as far as feels comfortable for your hips and back.

limitations: No automatic power, impact, or advanced technique scoring.

name: Guard Return
purpose: Build the habit of bringing your hands back to a relaxed guard after each movement.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear floor. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise without contact and at a slow pace. Stop if uncomfortable.
instructions: Start in a comfortable boxing stance with hands in guard.
Let one hand move slightly away from the face.
Bring it straight back to guard.
Pause, check your balance, then repeat with the other hand.
commonCues: Return to the same guard position each time.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Bring the hand back up near the face before moving again.
Breathe out and let the shoulders relax.

limitations: Guided practice. Return-to-guard cues will only be enabled after validation.

name: Forward & Backward Footwork
purpose: Practise small, balanced steps forwards and backwards from your stance.
space: At least 3 m of clear, non-slip floor in front of and behind you.
safety: Use a clear, non-slip floor and small steps. Stop if you feel unsteady or uncomfortable.
instructions: Start in a comfortable boxing stance.
Step the front foot forward a short distance, then let the back foot follow.
Step the back foot backward a short distance, then let the front foot follow.
Keep the same stance width after each step.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the feet roughly hip-width apart and let the lead foot move first.
Shorten the step so you stay balanced.

limitations: Timer and instructions only. Footwork is not automatically scored.
